abstract: This paper presents a frequency modulation continuous wave (FMCW) C-band radar system with high sensitivity and 2D detection capacity to detect low-radar cross section targets and to measure their range, velocity and micro-Doppler signature. A low jitter high signal-to-noise and distortion ratio (SINAD) S band signal is directly generated by an SDR system based on Xilinx FPGA system, which greatly increases the micro-Doppler and angle estimation performance of the system. Up conversion to C-Band by x2 frequency multiplication is performed. Proper amplification and filtering of emitted and detected signals are implemented to achieve 80dB dynamic range in the final system. The transmitter and the receiver are mounted on a designed fixture to reduce the ground reflections and their crosstalk. The transmitter antenna is a single 90° width whereas multi-long baseline interferometer (MLBI) concept is implemented in the receiver antenna for a low cost, low dimension and high angle resolution in the 2D position of the targets. Measurements in terms of the range, the velocity and the micro Doppler signature of a small drone have been carried out to evaluate the proposed radar system. The results show that we can clearly detect, identify and track the small drone within a 500 m range, which demonstrates the high performance of the radar and its potential use for UAV tracking and identification.

articleTitle: THz ISAR Imaging of Space Target with Vibration Compensation
abstract: In spatial situational awareness (SSA), Terahertz (THz) inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) includes the characteristics of high-resolution imaging and all-day operation. However, compared with low-frequency ISAR, micro vibrations of space targets can cause images defocusing in THz band. Commonly, the existing vibration compensation algorithms performed time-frequency analysis on the echo data. Then, the vibration phase error was obtained and compensated. However, these techniques are limited to the prominent scattering point and are unable to address the intricate non-linear vibration of the space target. In response to this problems, an THz ISAR imaging framework with non-rigid vibration compensation is proposed. First, a compressed sensing (CS) model is developed to correct for phase error in ISAR imaging due to vibration. Subsequently, the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) is leveraged to optimize the CS model. It is important to note that the ISAR imaging algorithm is transformed into a 2D matrix form in order to reduce memory usage and improve computational efficiency. Finally, measured data is leveraged to validate the superiority of the proposed algorithm, demonstrating the potential of ISAR imaging for practical space targets.

articleTitle: Reliable Traffic Monitoring Using Low-Cost Doppler Radar Units
abstract: Road traffic monitoring typically involves the counting and recording of vehicles on public roads over extended periods. The data gathered from such monitoring provides useful information to municipal authorities in urban areas. This paper presents a low-cost, widely deployable sensing subsystem based on Continuous Wave Doppler radar. The proposed system can perform vehicle detection and speed estimation with a total cost of less than 100 USD. The sensing system (including the hardware subsystem and the algorithms) is designed to be placed on the side of the road, allowing for easy deployment and serviceability.

articleTitle: Determination of Absolute Interferometric Phase in Circular InSAR Based on Demons Algorithm and Dual-angle Observation
abstract: The generation of high-precision ground digital elevation models (DEMs) based on synthetic aperture radar interferometry (InSAR) technology has attracted wide attention. One main problem is the phase ambiguity in the generated interferogram. Without external DEM, the 360° aperture gives circular InSAR (In-CSAR) the capability to estimate the phase ambiguity. We present, for the first time, the combination of Demons algorithm and dual-angle observation for absolute interferometric phase determination of In-CSAR system. The proposed strategy can estimate the phase ambiguity by dual-angle DEMs registration.

articleTitle: Explaining SAR ATR Models Predictions with Counterfactual Explanations
abstract: In recent years, Deep Learning models have become more and more popular and their performance have been tested on several domains, from medical to military applications. While being particularly competitive, their non-transparency nature raise plentiful questions, in particular in critical applications for which it seems self-evident to have more insight on models. To alleviate this issue, the eXplainable Artificial Intelligence field has emerged in order to propound more understandable models and consequently to make them more trustworthy. Yet, eXplainable Artificial Intelligence for Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images and especially for Automatic Target Recognition (ATR) is still an emerging subject. In this paper, we investigate the potential of counterfactual explanations to explain ATR model decisions. Not only do we detail the method that we used to generate counterfactual explanations, but we also illustrate how we exploit them to provide semi-global explanations. Thanks to the well-known MSTAR dataset, we effectively show that this approach can unveil how the model imagines a class against another and, more generally, improve the comprehension of the ATR model reasoning.

articleTitle: Covariance Estimation of Generalized Monopulse for Radar Tracking
abstract: Generalized Monopulse is an asymptotically efficient estimator of the Direction of Arrival (DoA), offering manifold array processing such as anti-jamming through adaptive beamforming, or clutter cancellation through space-time adaptive processing. In addition, this estimator is unbiased even in the general case of arbitrary antenna arrays, making it preferable over classical monopulse techniques. Its performance is well predicted in analytical formulae which are unfortunately inconvenient for real-time applications. Indeed, the unknown covariance matrix of the DoA estimation is usually required to tune the tracking stage, such as Kalman filters, for instance. This paper proposes a simple estimator for the covariance matrix of Generalized Monopulse intended for real time processing.

articleTitle: Improving Deep Learning Change Detection in Automotive Radar Maps by Data Augmentation
abstract: In this paper, we deal with the task of change detection for environment maps based on automotive radar sensors. As our main contribution, map misalignment common in the real world due to bad positioning is taken into account as part of the prediction. The data augmentation strategies proposed in this paper imparts the knowledge of rotation and translation invariance into the baseline convolutional neural network based siamese architecture, trained with radar maps of highway scenes focusing on construction zones on the road. Using our proposed strategies, our model outperformed the baseline by attaining 18% and 13% higher average F1 scores with respect to rotational and translational misalignments.

articleTitle: Experimental Results on Co-registration for Multitemporal ICEYE SAR Images
abstract: In this paper, we present experimental results on SAR image co-registration. The simple-coregistration method does not requires information on coordinates of flights, ground scene and so on. Two reference samples in each SAR image that can be easily selected are what the method requires. The method is based on re-sampling SAR images with respect to a selected image plane. The re-sampling was performed based on 2-D fast Fourier transform and cubic spline 2D interpolation. The experimental results in multitemporal data with ICEYE satellite data show an increase in the coherence magnitude between the images after the co-registration method. Namely, the coherence increases about three times after co-registration in a particular setting.

articleTitle: An Estimation-Theoretic Approach to Joint Antenna Placement and Power Allocation in Colocated MIMO Radar
abstract: MIMO radar systems offer significant performance improvements but come with challenges in terms of hardware costs and processing complexity. In this work, we propose a joint antenna placement and power allocation (JAPPA) scheme based on an estimation-theoretic approach to cope with such challenges. We formulate an optimization problem to minimize the number of antennas while bounding a scalar metric of the Cramer-Rao Lower Bound (CRLB) matrix for a two-target scenario. The problem is cast as a convex optimization problem, which can be efficiently solved. Computer simulations validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach in reducing the number of antennas as well as the total power while meeting performance requirements with respect to a benchmark design.

Author Keywords: joint antenna placement and power allocation

articleTitle: Sub-Surface and Remote Sensing Stand Testing Using Stepped-Frequency Continuous Wave Signals
abstract: The laboratory stand was tested for subsurface and remote sensing research using the AD8302 amplitude-phase detector and stepped-frequency continuous wave signals. The schematic diagram of the stand and its components was described and presented. Amplitude and phase of radio wave images were obtained for the cases of tested object shallowly buried in dry sand and positioned on its surface in the laboratory conditions. The results will be used in future works to realize measurement techniques for detecting different type landmines at the base of electromagnetic sensors installed in the unmanned aerial vehicles.

articleTitle: Simulation of buried objects Radar Cross Section (RCS) using a Hybrid Finite Volume Method: Experimental validation through RCS measurements of a PEC sphere
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative hybrid finite volume method designed to assess the Radar Cross Section (RCS) of buried objects exposed to a plane wave. The study includes a comprehensive experimental validation of this method, involving a specific experiment tailored to evaluate its performance. The article outlines the fundamental principles of the numerical scheme and offers a detailed description of the experimental setup. Furthermore, it includes a comparative analysis between simulation results and actual measurements.

articleTitle: Detection of Power Increasing Noise-Like Smart Jammers
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of detecting a Noise-Like Jammer (NLJ) that gradually increases the transmitted power, rather than quickly transmitting all the available one. This power control strategy can bypass conventional electronic countermeasures, since classical methods are based on the detection of a noise power discontinuity in the window under test (WUT). To address this issue, we recently proposed two novel NLJ detection architectures by assuming specific models for NLJ power variation during the design stage. The first model is based on a linear law for NLJ power variation over the observation time. In contrast, the second model supposes unconstrained fluctuations in the NLJ power within the WUT. To test these hypotheses, we have made ad hoc modifications of the generalized likelihood ratio test, where the unknown parameters are estimated through iterative procedures. The performance analysis, conducted using synthetic data, demonstrates the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed detectors over the conventional approach. Moreover, we show that one of the proposed detectors returns a constant false alarm rate for a wide range of noise power levels, whereas the probability of false alarm for the other detector is lower than the nominal one when the noise power level changes.

articleTitle: Iterative Capon Estimation for Saturated Forward Jamming Suppression with MIMO Radar
abstract: We discuss the iterative Capon estimation (ICE) method for saturated forward jamming suppression with multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar in this paper. The amplitude envelope of MIMO angular return echo is different from the jamming signal in a saturated mode. The ICE in this paper utilizes the Capon estimation initialization algorithm. The algorithm estimates amplitude and phase estimations of both the jamming signal and the real echo along range within a single snapshot, exploiting the waveform differences. And it uses eclipsing repair to estimate parameters in the eclipsed region. The simulation results prove that the ICE method can effectively suppress the forward jamming signal and identify the real target.

articleTitle: Differentiating Tsunamis from Atmospheric-Induced Events Using Coastal High-Frequency Radars
abstract: On October 14, 2016, a real-time tsunami warning was automatically issued by the High-Frequency radar of Tofino, on the west coast of British Columbia, Canada. This warning was based on the observation of an anomalous pattern in surface currents traveling towards the shore. However, subsequent analyses showed that this event was more likely an atmospheric-induced phenomenon than a "real" tsunami. In this paper, we investigate the use of wind direction inferred from HF measurements to differentiate in real-time between genuine tsunamis and "tsunami-like" events resulting from severe atmospheric conditions.

articleTitle: The 3D-MAGIC project : Design and production of electromagnetic absorbers using 3D printing
abstract: The main objective of the 3D-MAGIC project was to design and manufacture absorbers in the microwave range (2 to 20 GHz), using a lossy materials structuring approach and additive manufacturing. The project was divided into three different phases. The first one involved the building of a "Materials" database, by defining compositions and measuring electromagnetic properties. The second one was to design and simulate structured broadband absorbers. The third phase dealt with the experimental validation of 3D-printed RF absorbers with a selected composite. In the end, two demonstrators were produced and featured expected performances in terms of absorption in the desired frequency range.

articleTitle: Protection of Critical Infrastructure using LTE450-based Passive Radar: Range Measurements for Drone Detection
abstract: Considering the massively increasing importance of drones in actual military conflicts or potential terrorist attacks in conjunction with the vulnerability of critical infrastructure against these kinds of threats, early drone detection is a key issue and particularly challenging for non-emitting drones. In Germany and other European countries a blackout resistant LTE network in the 450 MHz band for critical infrastructure sites is currently rolled outed or already planned. The basestation transmitters are presumably well suited as illuminators in a passive radar setup for drone detection.In this contribution we present experimental results for range measurements with a LTE450-based passive radar for drone detection. An experimental comparison of horizontal versus vertical polarization of the reception antenna as well as different direct path cancellation algorithms is included.

articleTitle: 120 GHz and 240 GHz Si-Ge FMCW radar for high resolution close range SAR imaging
abstract: A 3D close range Synthetic Aperture Radar system based on the Range Migration Algorithm and working with affordable and compact Si-Ge Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave radar units is presented. The two radar sensors operates at 120 GHz with 19.5 GHz bandwidth and at 240 GHz with 34 GHz bandwidth. A new method for enhancing lateral resolution combined with a normalization procedure is proposed, leading to 0.33 central wavelength resolution for the 120 GHz radar transceiver and 0.47 for the 240 GHz radar unit. Lateral resolution is compared to a conventional focused beam imaging system. Objects of interest are displayed to reveal Synthetic Aperture Radar advantages in term of lateral resolution and depth of field for Non Destructive Testing and inspection purposes.

articleTitle: Target Localisation in Real Time for Non-Coherent Multistatic Passive Radar
abstract: A real-time passive radar system has been developed, and a three node multistatic configuration has been constructed for the purpose of target localisation. The target localisation process refers to converting a target from radar coordinates to geographic coordinates. A typical passive radar will use the delay estimate of a target along with an angle estimate from a phased array, to estimate the geographic coordinates of the target. The alternative approach is having multiple receive/transmit nodes providing a delay estimate of the same target, then computing the intersections of target ellipsoids to estimate the target location. This paper demonstrates a real-time system to perform target localisation on three spatially separated passive radar nodes. A formulation is presented which does not rely on a common transmitter or receiver in the network. A number of numerical target localisation algorithms are presented and demonstrated using both a common transmitter, and with two spatially separated transmitters. The accuracy of these algorithms are compared against truth data.

articleTitle: Real-Time Bistatic Noise Radar with Adaptive Beamforming
abstract: Implementing continuous wave noise radar systems has long been hindered by detrimental self-interference, severely limiting the systems’ detection sensitivity. We experimentally demonstrate the advantage of bistatic separation and adaptive beamforming in suppressing self-interference. The bistatic system operates in real-time and can detect small UAVs at ranges of more than 3.2 km. Increasing the output power or antenna gain will extend the detection range as self-interference does not limit the system; thermal noise does.

articleTitle: SWOT Cal/Val Campaign based on the SWALIS airborne sensor. Comparaison of σ0 over the Rhine
abstract: This paper introduces a quick comparison of backscattering coefficients, denoted as σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, between data gathered by the SWALIS (Still Water Low Incidence Scattering) airborne sensor and those from the SWOT (Surface Water and Ocean Topography) satellite mission. These comparisons were conducted over two distinct locations over the Rhine : Plobsheim and Gerstheim. SWALIS reveals fluctuations in these coefficients both in the open expanses and in areas adjacent to the banks over Plobsheim areas.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Approach to Helicopter Open set Classification based on Microdoppler Signatures
abstract: Detecting and identifying rotorcrafts is a critical challenge in the domains of defense and security. Helicopters, due to their low speed and altitude, pose unique difficulties in radar-based detection. Moreover, accurate identification is strategically important. Thankfully, helicopters’ radar return signals are modulated with characteristic frequencies directly related to the rotary motion of their rotors. Leveraging this micro-Doppler radar signature, in addition to existing sensors, can significantly enhance the detection and classification performance. In this article, we explore the application of neural network-based algorithms to identify rotorcraft in an open-set context, accounting for scenarios where samples could belong to unknown classes as in an operational scenario.

articleTitle: Standardization of Residuals for Detection of Unknown Target Classification of SAR images
abstract: The recent advancements in deep learning architectures have enabled the efficient and accurate classification of pre-trained targets in SAR images. However, encountering unknown targets during testing scenarios is unavoidable, causing misclassification and subsequently compromising classifier accuracy. Over the past few decades, a variety of approaches have been developed to address this challenge, yet the detection of unknown targets shows unstable fluctuations of accuracy dependent on the decision threshold value and the number of unknown targets. In this context, we propose a standardized method that demonstrates a relatively stable detection rate across multiple unknown target conditions concerning threshold metrics. As an example, we demonstrate feature extraction from the latent space of a deep learning network. Using these feature representations, residuals are computed from training data samples and then fitted with a Gaussian distribution to estimate statistical parameters. Anderson-Darling statistics are then applied to delineate the decision boundary for unknown targets. Furthermore, the comparison of histogram percentiles between known and unknown target classes is taken into account for establishing the fine-tuned statistical threshold for filtering unknown target samples. This systematic process consistently filters out unknown target classes across varying quantities of unknown classes at a fixed threshold value. Finally, we argue the practical significance of our approach within realistic scenarios.

articleTitle: Low Probability of Interception Radar Signals Detection, Comparison of a YOLOv8 Model and a Conventional Signal Processing Method
abstract: Radar interception plays a critical role in electronic warfare by capturing and analyzing enemy radar emissions. Low Probability of Intercept (LPI) signals pose a significant challenge to conventional detection methods due to their design to minimize detectability. This paper explores the benefit of the YOLOv8 algorithm, a state-of-the-art deep learning model, for detecting LPI radar signals in time-frequency images. A comparative analysis to assess detection performance is conducted with a common sense solution based on energy detector which is the Generalized Likelihood Ratio Test (GLRT) when the signal is unknown. Results demonstrate that YOLOv8 achieves detection with a notable improvement in Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) for every waveform considered.

articleTitle: Composite metasurface for surface wave radar enhancement
abstract: This paper presents the design, fabrication and experimental validation of a compact composite metasurface for surface wave radar. The aim is to enhance the efficiency of such system by modifying the radiation characteristics of the emitting antenna with a highly inductive metasurface.

articleTitle: Investigation on Micromotion Characteristics of Trimaran and Corner Reflector Based on the Motion of Six Degrees of Freedom
abstract: A trimaran is an advanced ship with high hydrodynamic performance, the study of its electromagnetic (EM) scattering characteristics in marine environments is of value to the detection of trimaran ships. This paper presents a method to evaluate the effect of corner reflectors on the scattering field of a trimaran. Based on the Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) equations, the interpolation wave-making method (IWMM) is proposed for the prediction of the six degrees of freedom (6-DOF) motion of the trimaran and corner reflectors. This method takes into account the viscous effect of the flow field and the complexity of wave motion, which can be applied to the seakeeping prediction of ships under different sea states. Second, the influence of corner reflectors on the backscattering characteristics of the ship-sea scene is demonstrated by the geometrical optics and physical optics (GO-PO) algorithm. Finally, the Doppler spectrum characteristics of the composite scene are presented by the standard spectrum estimation method, which provides a reference for radar detection and identification of ships in the microwave band.

articleTitle: Microlocal Analysis of Multistatic Radar Imaging
abstract: We consider the synthetic aperture radar experiment in which waves, simultaneously emitted from a pair of stationary emitters, are scattered by objects and measured by a receiver that makes multiple passes over the scattering region. In such problems, the possibility for passive, background signals to be recorded during a radar experiment and corrupt the image is often neglected. Our work addresses this by considering the two emitters to be ‘always on’ so there is the potential for ‘crosstalk’ between their signals. Closely related is the problem of passive imaging, where one wishes to produce a high-quality image purely from background signals, for which our analysis is also applicable.We use a single-scattering model for the radar data recorded from two emitters and assume that the data cannot be separated. Backprojection of the data leads to artifacts and we determine their positions in the image relative to the scatterers that produced them. We develop two methods that mitigate these artifacts; a technique utilising a carefully designed data acquisition geometry and an image processing technique that displaces artifacts away from a region of interest (ROI). We describe the necessary conditions for these methods to be applicable and discuss their limitations.

articleTitle: Ship-borne 3D ISAR Imaging
abstract: Interest in three-dimensional (3D) radar imaging of non-cooperative targets is growing fast. Recent results have clearly shown that there is a significant improvement with respect to traditional two-dimensional radar imaging as it provides the means to produce accurate and robust target classification and recognition. Moreover, more recently, various demonstrators have been built to produce valid evidence of the technology feasibility and advancement in terms of technology readiness level (TRL). This paper shows results relative to the development of a ship-borne dual-mode radar system, able to switch between standard surveillance mode and 2D/3D InISAR mode upon user request. This system may potentially enhance the surveillence capabilities of ships by enabling not only detection, but also imaging and recognition of non-cooperative targets. This paper presents both the theoretical aspects related to the 3D ISAR image formation, specifically for the ship-borne case, and experimental validation results, obtained by collecting data with the system demonstrator. As the system demonstrator has not yet been installed on a ship, the results will be limited to the case of a ground-based-equivalent installation. The system’s ability to generate 3D radar images of moving surface targets is demonstrated by applying the developed algorithms to data collected in a relevant scenario with targets of opportunity.

articleTitle: Passive Multistatic Localization with the Prior Receiving Beamwidth Constraint
abstract: This paper investigates the target localization using bistatic range measurements with multiple transmitters and one passive receiver. We introduce an angular constraint to incorporate the valuable information from the main-lobe beamwidth of the receiving antenna into the passive multistatic localization problem. Then, a specific Semidefinite Relaxation (SDR) based algorithm is proposed to tackle this quadratically constrained quadratic programming (QCQP) problem. Simulation results illustrate that the proposed algorithm effectively leverages the prior main-lobe beamwidth information, resulting in lower estimation errors compared to alternative methods.

articleTitle: Micro-Doppler Super-Resolution Using Iterative Adaptive Approach
abstract: Micro-Doppler signatures refer to the time-varying Doppler frequency modulation induced by the motion of multiple parts or features of a target or scene, in addition to the bulk motion of the target. Radar experts have extensively utilized micro-Doppler signatures to identify targets displaying micro-motions. The short-time Fourier transform (STFT) is commonly employed for extracting micro-Doppler signatures in radar applications. The STFT is designed to enhance either temporal or spectral resolution or to achieve a balance between them. In this paper, we introduce the application of Doppler super-resolution utilizing the Iterative Adaptive Approach (IAA) method, commonly employed for angle estimation. The proposed technique enhances temporal resolution by achieving super-resolution in Doppler estimation while utilizing a reduced number of samples for the spectral domain. This technique is applied to generate spectrograms with finer resolutions, aiming to improve the performance of micro-Doppler classification methods. This paper demonstrates the enhanced performance of micro-Doppler classification achieved with IAA through analysis of real radar data.

articleTitle: High-Frequency Surface Wave Radars in the Mediterranean Sea: civil and environmental applications
abstract: The Mediterranean Institute of Oceanography (MIO) has been operating for one decade a network of high-frequency radars for the monitoring of coastal surface currents on the French Mediterranean coast. More recently, ONERA has been developing an original over-the-horizon radar system for the detection and tracking of ships in the coastal zone. The two institutions have joined their efforts to provide dual civil and environmental applications of surface wave radars in the framework of the ROSMED project. We present preliminary results of the unique capabilities of the ONERA radar for the mapping of surface currents at very long range in the Gulf of Lion. We also present new results of the MIO high-frequency radar for the measurement of surface currents and waves and the automatic detection of ships.

articleTitle: Multi-Sensor Data Fusion Based on Millimeter Radar and Laser Disdrometer
abstract: This paper is devoted to discussing peculiarities of multi-instrument measurements of rain using millimeter band radar and laser optical disdrometers as basic sensors with application of weather station and radiometer as sources of additional information. After brief discussion of meteorological radar application for quantitative information obtaining, the paper considers the problems and their possible solutions in respect to data fusion and comparison the results of measurements with sensors of different physical nature. 94 GHz radar, laser optical disdrometers, weather station and potentially the radiometer are considered as information sources. Experimental part of the research is based on measurements of rain provided during several years at the experimental range located in Cabauw, the Netherlands. Specialized MATLAB software with friendly interface is developed for this sophisticated processing and used for fusion and comparison of 94 GHz radar data with non-radar synchronous data

articleTitle: Bio-inspired Waveform in a Multistatic Configuration
abstract: Waveform diversity is a topic of major interest in the context of multistatic radar. This paper presents a bio-inspired waveform in order to potentially broaden the range of available waveforms. In particular, we aim at transmitting several waveforms in the same band, while maintaining the radar performances. The performances of systems transmitting the proposed waveform or different chirp-based waveforms is assessed by measuring the isolation level, Doppler tolerance and sidelobe levels. Improvements in the sidelobe levels of the considered waveforms are discussed with the application of the mismatched filter and its influence on the isolation properties and Doppler tolerance.

articleTitle: Federated Learning for Radar Systems - Sharing Knowledge without sharing Data
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a technique that was introduced by Google in the area of Internet of Things (IoT) as a privacy preserving way of using user data in the training of their neural networks [1]. The core element of FL is a distributed learning algorithm that runs in local clients, e.g. phones or computers, and uses data stored on these devices. After this local training, the models trained on the clients are uploaded onto a server, which performs a model aggregation, e.g. by averaging the model parameters, and creates a new global model that is again distributed to the clients. This process is continuously repeated to improve the model performance over time and in this way the clients benefit from each other without sharing their data. In this paper, this learning scheme is proposed for radar networks and radar systems in general. This principle has some advantages since data, which might be confidential, does not have to be shared. Another possible application is that customers of a company benefit from each other when a common model is aggregated and redistributed among the customers using the learning results of all customers. A proof of concept example is presented using data compression by an autoencoder network.

articleTitle: Identifiability Analysis of Non-Integer Antenna Arrays in the Presence of Mixed (Strong and Weak) Signals
abstract: In this paper, we consider the direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation problem using a non-integer antenna array, and our objective is to examine the effect of sensor placement on the number of array degrees-of-freedom (DOFs) in the presence of a mixture of strong and weak signals. Two scenarios corresponding to off-grid sensor placement are considered: (1) when a single sensor of a uniform linear array (ULA) is in an off-grid position and (2) when the entire ULA is compressed. The smallest signal-subspace eigenvalue corresponding to the weak signals is compared with the rank-revealing QR factorization-based threshold that separates the signal subspace from the noise subspace, providing insights into the numerical rank of the data covariance matrix and serving as a measure of the DOFs of the array. Furthermore, the effect of signal strength on the eigenvalues of the data covariance matrix is studied. The effect of off-grid sensor placement and the variation of the signal strengths on the array DOFs is demonstrated with simulation results.

articleTitle: Improving Doppler Robustness for Optimized Complementary FM Waveform Subsets
abstract: In theory, complementary sequences are known to provide no sidelobes in the ideal scenario of zero-Doppler scattering and a distortionless transmitter. Since these conditions are not realistic in practice, a random frequency modulation (RFM) design approach was developed based on the notion of independent complementary subsets, where the FM nature mitigates some of unavoidable transmitter distortion and subset independence facilitates incoherent sidelobe averaging as a backup to complementary cancellation.While this complementary FM approach demonstrated greater resilience compared to theoretical codes (e.g. Golay), it did still only address zero-Doppler. Here, a generalization of that method is developed to enable complementary cancellation over a prescribed Doppler band. Simulation and open-air demonstration of these robust complementary FM waveforms validates that complementary sidelobe cancellation is preserved under Doppler effects.

articleTitle: 2D Spatial-Temporal Simulation of GPR Penetration in the 200-400MHz Band for Detecting Voids and Entrapped Persons in Multi-Layered Collapsed Building Structure
abstract: This paper presents a foundational framework towards designing a portable, site-specific radar system for use in building collapse scenarios, focusing on the detection of voids beneath debris and analyzing GPR signals for locating hidden survivors. To analyze GPR signal characteristics, we employed the Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method, utilizing simulation tools such as gprMax and High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS) to model electromagnetic wave propagation within intricate multilayered debris structures. This paper examines the GPR A-scan, B-scan(radargram) and signal propagations across various configurations of collapse site structures, ranging from solely soil compositions to those incorporating thin or thick concrete and wooden layers, each with embedded voids and entrapped persons inside voids.This work aims to enhance the efficiency of survivor search and rescue operations at collapse sites, laying down a theoretical basis for validating experiments designed by real-world collapse scenarios. By scrutinizing the influence of GPR's operating frequency and the structural composition of debris on detection performance, the findings serve as crucial foundational data for tailoring GPR design and understanding detection characteristics pertinent to real-world conditions.

articleTitle: Radar/Optro Meta-sensor: Augmented Radar Tracking Performances by Adaptive Camera Resources Allocation
abstract: This paper proposes a radar/optro meta sensor in which auxiliary cameras help one main radar to track the targets it detects and to continue tracking in case the radar loses one track. We present two approaches on real data to mitigate the radar track loss with the support of one auxiliary camera in a single target scenario. We investigate multi-target tracking with intermittent support of two cameras in a similar setting on simulated data.

articleTitle: Classification of Radar Pulses Modulation Laws via Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: This article takes place in the context of Electronic Warfare Support (EWS). The intended objective is to establish a superheterodyne receiver in order to detect potential threats. Because a superheterodyne receiver cannot listen to a wide frequency bandwidth, we suggest establishing a scan strategy that focuses more frequently on unknown radar signals. For this purpose, we propose a method to classify the radar signals in order to know if we already received the signal of a given source. We focus on pulse feature extraction and more specifically on classification of the modulation law. The idea is to be robust to other parameters like pulse length or Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR). We select signal representations which conserve the time dimension like raw signal and time-frequency representations and apply Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to extract automatically the important features. Based on simulations carried out, we finally conclude that both representations offer similar results for SNR between 0 and 5 dB. We also notice that phase modulated pulses are the most difficult to distinguish. They are confused with each other. The amplitude modulated pulses can also be confused with simple pulses. The chosen frequency modulated signals are the easiest to classify.

articleTitle: TS-SCAN: a Density-Based Clustering Method for Trajectory Analysis and Anomaly Detection
abstract: The surging amount of trajectories from sensors, antennas, and radars calls for the development of modern trajectory analysis techniques. In this context, we have introduced 2 ways to compare trajectories, which include a regularisation for dynamic time warping (DTW) and a faster computation of the Fréchet distance. As an example, we present TS-SCAN, an extension of the DBSCAN algorithm, which computes trajectory clusters and their average scheme in a database.

articleTitle: A Novel Radar Forward-Looking Three-Dimensional Imaging Algorithm on Moving Platform Based on Vortex Electromagnetic Wave
abstract: Vortex electromagnetic waves (VEMW) have unique wavefront phase modulation characteristics. As a new freedom of degree in diversity for radar transmitter, the VEMW radar (VEMWR) can yield radar cross-section (RCS) diversity, improve signal and information processing dimensions and performance. The detection and imaging performance of VEMWR has been verified in various radar systems. This article focuses on the imaging application of forward-looking radar imaging on moving platform, and proposes a multiple-mode scanning method for large imaging field of view based on a uniform circular array (UCA) system. Next, an improved two-dimensional (2D) back-projection and range-doppler algorithm (BP-RD) is proposed, utilizing the difference of magnitude and Doppler frequency at different elevation of multi-mode VEMW and phase difference at different azimuth angles, to achieve 3D imaging of the target. Due to the VEMW 's energy divergence, as the elevation angle increases, the beam pattern gain of the high-mode VEMW decreases sharply. The proposed method can effectively improve the signal processing gain by utilizing the energy distribution of multiple modes in the spatial domain. Based on the imaging results of the point target, it was verified that the normalized gain of target imaging results is basically equivalent either at low or high elevation within the multi-mode VEMW field of view, the algorithm exhibits outstanding stability.

articleTitle: Orbital Angular Momentum Based Monopulse Angle Estimation against Cross-eye Jamming
abstract: Cross-eye jamming exhibits significant threat against current monopulse radars. In this work, a novel method based on orbital angular momentum evaluation is proposed for robust monopulse angle estimation against cross-eye jamming. The direction of arrival of the incident electromagnetic field is estimated with the spatial gradients of the orbital angular momentum topological charge distribution in the radar plane. The mathematical modeling as well as the numerical simulations are performed. According to the results, the angular estimation errors with our proposal is much lower compared with the traditional approach based on amplitude comparison in presence of cross-eye jamming.

articleTitle: Phase Synchronization of Distributed Array Radar based on Minimum Entropy Method
abstract: Distributed array radar (DAR) coherently fuse multiple small-aperture subarrays, achieving equivalent resolution of a large aperture, which enables significant benefits for automotive driving, remote sensing and other applications. However, individual oscillators and coarse synchronization system induced phase deviation breaks the array spatial uniform sampling. To address this problem, a minimization entropy based DAR phase synchronization method is proposed to fuse the measurements of multiple subarrays. First we establish an connection between phase deviations and the uncertainty of spatial spectrum shape through information entropy. Then phase deviation required for synchronization is estimated by iteratively optimizing the entropy value to minimum. Simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method and indicate that phase corrected DAR possesses high noise suppression and high angular resolution.

articleTitle: Joint Design of Transmit Waveform and Receive Filter for Deceptive Jammer Suppression with FDA-MIMO Radar
abstract: This paper considers the joint design of transmit waveform and receive filter for FDA-MIMO radar in the presence of the deceptive jammers. In our system design, the problem is formulated to maximize the Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR) while incorporating constant modulus and similarity constraints. Specifically, for the emerged non-convex waveform optimization problem, an iterative algorithm based on the Majorization-Minimization (MM) framework is proposed to approximate the optimal solution. Furthermore, a projection algorithm is developed to eliminate the constraints. Finally, numerical simulation results illustrate that the proposed method can efficiently suppress the deceptive jammers by evaluating the SINR performance, similarity to the reference waveform, and beampattern.

articleTitle: AMBRA project: cooperative multistatic radar for aerial target detection in urban areas
abstract: Surveillance of low-altitude airspace in urban areas raises a number of challenges: the size of the areas to be monitored, the presence of buildings that can mask certain parts of the city, the terrain and the difficulty of identifying sites with sufficient clearance make it difficult to use conventional radars. Recent years have seen the emergence and rapid growth in the use of remote-controlled or autonomous drones equipped with control systems that enable them to fly at low altitude and low speed. Numerous solutions have been proposed for detecting them in open areas, but there are still few effective means of detecting them in urban areas. This difficulty will be even greater in the "city of the future", when we want to detect autonomous delivery drones or "flying taxi" projects proposed to relieve urban road traffic congestion. The AMBRA (Active Multistatic Broadcast RAdar) project proposes a new approach based on an existing infrastructure that is already capable of covering the entire urban area.

articleTitle: Lightweight pod design for radar threat emitter simulation
abstract: Specifications, design, manufacture and preliminary testing of a pod-mounted radar-like transmitter for training fighter pilots to react to Radar Warning Receiver alarms generated from a low-cost but representative device for red forces.

articleTitle: Radar Prehistory
abstract: This paper describes some of the earliest studies and experiments which laid the foundations for the development of radar, covering the years from the mid 19th century through to the start of WW2.

articleTitle: Experimental Demo of Range Disambiguation via Slow-time Coding & Reiterative Super-Resolution
abstract: Slow-time coding (STC) has previously been examined for MIMO radar and disambiguation of multiple range ambiguities. Using STC with non-adaptive Doppler processing often results in high Doppler "cross-ambiguity" sidelobes that can severely hinder range disambiguation despite the degree of separability imparted by STC. To enhance this separability, a "multi-range" modification to the reiterative super-resolution (RISR) approach is examined that accounts for the distinct range interval structure from STC and is denoted as MR-RISR. The efficacy of this implementation is examined using open-air measurements. Further, incorporation of clutter cancellation via the previously developed background supplementary cancellation (BaSC) arrangement is shown to yield further improvement by reducing the necessary dynamic range for which Doppler estimation is needed.

articleTitle: Filters Design that Mitigate Pulse Eclipsing Modulation of Pulse Agile Waveforms
abstract: When pulse agile waveforms are applied to moving target indication (MTI) and moving target detection (MTD) radars, they face the problem of range sidelobe modulation (RSM). Previous research has mainly focused on solving this problem by designing corresponding mismatched filters (MMFs). However, the effectiveness of MMFs will be compromised when pulse eclipsing occurs. In this paper, we propose a new method for designing MMFs and suppress the RSM caused by pulse eclipsing through segmented pulse compression with different MMFs. We mitigate the impact of pulse eclipsing by extracting close-range clutter information from the echo and incorporating it into the filters design process. Compared with the existing MMFs, the proposed filters can reduce RSM by 10–20 dB.

articleTitle: Platform for Direction of Arrival measurements considering complex scenario : Application to Radome Evaluation
abstract: This manuscript presents a platform called SAMBA dedicated to RADAR measurements. The platform is a completely modular receiver. This allows to obtain datas related to any devices at a level system by considering differential measurements. Indeed, the Direction of Arrival can be directly obtained instead of measuring S-parameters or radiation pattern. Twenty-four Rx modules are available which allow the measurements of quite complex antennas. In this paper, the platform is described and an example of application on radome performances is proposed.

articleTitle: Target Range and Velocity Estimation for Joint Radar and Communications with Up and Down Chirps
abstract: This paper proposes joint radar and communications scheme based on chirp waveform diversity. A monostatic radar transmits a sequence of alternating up and down chirps to acquire target related information (TRI), while leveraging such waveform diversity to deliver data to another radar. This data can be TRI acquired in previous coherent pulse interval (CPI) or scheduling data, such as radar signal bandwidth, carrier frequency, and waveform parameters. We propose range and velocity estimation of multiple targets using dechirping and discrete Fourier transform (DFT). Given P chirps and N fast time samples, 2N DFTs, each of length $\frac{P}{2}$, are computed over slow time to locate peaks in the corresponding DFT amplitudes. The most frequently occurring peak locations are utilized for estimating target velocities, which, together with most frequently occurring peak locations in 2P DFTs, each of length $\frac{N}{2}$, computed over fast time, are then used for estimating target ranges. When compared to the standard range-Doppler processing, this method reduces computational complexity, and is motivated for improving robustness against noise. Computer simulations are used to show the performance of the proposed method in terms of the range and velocity estimation errors versus signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Simulations show that the proposed method provides better range estimation than the method that uses only up or down chirps, especially when two targets are closely located. These results suggest that alternating up and down chirp-based transmission not only supports data transmission but also improves radar performance.

articleTitle: Field-trial Demonstration of a Broadband Microwave Photonic TDM-MIMO Radar
abstract: A microwave photonic time division multiplexing (TDM) multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) radar is demonstrated in which photonic frequency quadrupling is applied to generate broadband radar signals and photonic frequency mixing is applied to implement de-chirp processing of the radar echoes. To enable TDM transmission, a radio frequency switch is used to control the signal in different channels. In the receiver, an effective transceiver connection architecture based on multi-channel optical reference signals is adopted to realize the aliasing-free processing of all the radar echoes. Thanks to the wide radar bandwidth and large virtual aperture size, this microwave photonic TDM-MIMO radar is capable to realize high-resolution target imaging with deep suppression of grating lobes. Performance of the proposed microwave photonic TDM-MIMO radar is investigated through field-trial experiments, in which the established radar has a 6×8 linear antenna array and a bandwidth of 8 GHz (10-18 GHz) in each channel. Using broadband digital beamforming with scanning time delay compensation, high-resolution imaging of a reflector mounted on an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) is achieved. In the obtained image, the range resolution and angular resolution of the radar are estimated to be 1.95 cm and 0.2°, respectively, and the grating lobes are well suppressed because of the broadband angular dispersion effect.

articleTitle: Noise Radar Waveform Design: Preliminary Results for a MOEA Approach
abstract: Radar systems have obtained a lot of attention in recent years since they can operate in a variety of weather conditions and their applications are innumerable, ranging from automotive and marine radar to imaging or health monitoring purposes. Hence, noise radars have become a viable substitute for traditional radar technology, particularly in the defence domain. These systems excel for its resistance to jamming, low mutual interference and low probability of interception. However, the nature of non-deterministic sequences introduce several challenges such as fluctuations in the range sidelobes of the autocorrelation function, causing it to have a high sidelobe level, which can mask targets of interest. This paper introduces the use of Multi Objective Evolutionary Algorithms (MOEAs) to design noise radar waveforms with good correlation properties while maintaining an adequate efficiency at the power amplifier.

articleTitle: Investigation of a 3D MIMO TDM FMCW Radar
abstract: The proposed paper deals with 3D MIMO (multiple-input-multiple-output) TDM (time-division multiplexing) based on FMCW (frequency modulated continuous wave) radar. The basics of conventional FMCW radar are reviewed in order to introduce the principle of MIMO TDM (with "virtual antenna array"). Theoretical expressions of signals from the different "virtual antennas" in a 3D configuration, i.e. allowing to determine the angles (colatitude and longitude) in spherical coordinates, are demonstrated in detail. In this configuration, the transmit antennas are arranged in the plane xOz/yOz and the receive antennas in the axis Ox/Oy. The proposed developments are validated by simulation results at 60 GHz with error quatification.

articleTitle: A New wide-swath imaging and ground moving-target imaging scheme for MIMO-SAR based on azimuth phase coding*
abstract: In this study, a new wide-swath imaging and ground moving-target imaging (GMTIm) scheme was proposed based on azimuth phase coding (APC) for multiple-input multiple-output synthetic aperture radar (MIMO-SAR) systems. The new scheme transmitted multiple APC waveforms to different sub-regions of a scene for simultaneous imaging, converted range ambiguity into Doppler ambiguity, used azimuth digital beamforming (DBF) to suppress range ambiguity in static scenes, and employed elevation DBF to suppress range ambiguity of moving targets. Finally, imaging space time adaptive processing (ISTAP) was applied to each unambiguous sub-region to obtain imaging results for moving targets in wide swath. The main advantages of the proposed scheme include the suppression of range-ambiguous clutter and ambiguous moving targets via two-dimensional DBF, reduction of the influence of height fluctuations in the range direction on ambiguity suppression, and multiple range resolutions in different sub-regions. Furthermore, the feasibility of the proposed scheme was verified through theoretical analysis and simulations.

articleTitle: High Accuracy DOA Estimation Based on Distributed 2D Nested Array
abstract: To improve the estimation accuracy of two-dimensional (2D) direction-of-arrival (DOA) of uniform rectangular array, and increase the degrees of freedom of the array, this paper proposes a novel array called distributed 2D nested array (DNRA). The DNRA consists of three 2D nested arrays, which greatly increase the degrees of freedom and the aperture of the array through sparse distribution of antenna elements and the distributed arrangement between subarrays. By using the proposed 2D Toeplitz matrix reconstruction algorithm, the estimation accuracy of the elevation angle and azimuth angle of the target is improved, and the computational cost of the algorithm is reduced. Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed array and algorithm.

articleTitle: Resolving Velocity Ambiguity via Virtual Error Compensation in Multi-Domain Coding Radar
abstract: This paper deals with the problem of resolving velocity ambiguity in Multi-Domain Coding (MDC) radar. At the modeling stage, the MDC radar is developed by coding in spatial, slow-time and fast-time domains. Specifically, the separation of the transmit signals in MDC radar is achieved through Doppler Division Multiple Access (DDMA), which reduces the maximum unambiguous velocity. Hence, the performance of detecting high-speed moving targets degrades. In order to solve this problem, a method based on virtual error compensation across the transmit antenna elements is developed. In particular, the velocity ambiguity index of the target is determined according to the minimum power of the received signals after beamforming because the virtual error is properly compensated. At the analysis stage, simulation results prove that the unambiguous velocity can be accurately estimated, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: First Results From Airborne Passive Radar Measurements And Aircraft Detection Exploiting Digital TV Broadcast Signals
abstract: New results of air-to-air target detection using airborne passive radar are presented. The detections are obtained by acquiring and processing data from an airborne passive sensor which receives DVB-T signals from digital-TV transmitters. The signal processing chain includes the following steps: decoding of the DVB-T signal, generation of a mismatched reference signal to suppress ambiguities, motion compensation and beam formation using three antenna channels for enhancing the signal-to-interference-and-noise ratio. A ground-based station is used to receive and demodulate the DVB-T signal in order to mitigate the large Doppler shifts of multi-path signals. The ground station data is synchronized to the airborne data using correlation techniques. An example result shows that a cooperative aircraft, located at 5 km distance, becomes detectable.

articleTitle: Adaptive Detectors for Moving Platform based Distributed Coherent Aperture Radar
abstract: Moving platform based distributed coherent aperture radar (MDCAR) is a promising technique for increasing gain, resolution, cost and flexibility. However, inherent grating lobes and coordination errors caused by large internode distance and moving platforms cause great trouble to target detection. To solve this problem, an array configuration accumulation (ACA) method is adopted. The time-varying platform motion is utilized to fill the spatial domain sampling. Then, according to the coherence between each array configuration, coherent accumulated detection (CAD) and non-coherent accumulated detection (NCAD) detectors are designed with robust steering vector estimation. Simulations are provided to validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Self-Supervised SAR Image Denoising Method for Ship Target Detection
abstract: In synthetic aperture radar (SAR) images, ship targets are easily submerged by complex background interference, and speckle noise causes blurring of ship edges, severely reducing image quality. This not only affects the usability of the images but also poses challenges for subsequent processing tasks such as image segmentation, target detection, and recognition. To address this issue, this paper proposes a self-supervised SAR image denoising method for ship target detection. This method extracts the regions of interest and suppresses the background in the image using a clustering-based mask. By combining a self-supervised learning strategy, the denoising network is trained only on noisy SAR data without the need for clean reference images, resulting in high-quality images. Experimental verification on GF3 data demonstrates the potential application of the proposed convolutional neural network in SAR image processing.

articleTitle: Width Measurement by Partial Convolution of Radar Signals in Spectral Domain
abstract: This work presents a width measurement system that jointly evaluates the signals gathered with two alternately transmitting radar modules that are placed laterally to the object of interest, one on each side. In both radar units, linear frequency-modulated continuous-waves are used as transmit signals. By applying a partial convolution to the resulting intermediate frequency (IF) signals in the spectral domain, the sum of the distances between the radar front ends and the target, and thus the object width is determined in one process step, which significantly reduces the calculation effort compared to individual evaluation of each radar’s data set. Furthermore, the introduced approach allows the use of previously known initial values of the object’s width, which may be used in case of filtering, since a lateral displacement of the target would only affect the individual distance estimates, but not their sum. Simulations as well as measurements in an indoor office environment using two 77GHz radar modules were performed to analyze the applicability and the accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Over-the-horizon surface wave radar: from the maritime target point-of-view
abstract: The work presented in this paper is part of an extensive study on HF surface wave radar, carried out jointly by ONERA and Sorbonne University for almost 20 years. In this article, we focus in particular on characterizing the maritime targets to be detected by this radar. To do this, we propose to use tools, both numerical and experimental, previously developed to characterize the radar's transmitting antennas: a numerical target model using equivalent sources, and instrumentation of a drone enabling near-field measurement of the field diffracted by the target. Finally, couplings between sky waves and surface waves on the target will be analyzed, enabling us to define a new Radar Cross Section, suitable for surface wave propagation.

articleTitle: Velocity Filtering Based Track-Before-Detect With Range And Doppler Ambiguities in Doppler Radars
abstract: Velocity filtering based track-before-detect has the strength of high energy integration efficiency and parameter estimation accuracy. However, conventional velocity filtering based approach may suffer from performance degradation due to the possible range and Doppler ambiguities in Doppler radars. In this paper, a new velocity filtering based track-before-detect method is proposed for multiframe weak target detection with ambiguous range and Doppler measurements. To deal with motion model mismatch in ambiguous range-Doppler plane, the accurate range-Doppler evolution with range and Doppler ambiguities is derived. It can be determined by the constant velocity, range and Doppler ambiguity factors of the target. Then, a complex pseudo-spectrum based velocity filtering track-before-detect method is proposed for weak target detection in ambiguous range-Doppler plane of Doppler radars. The constant target velocity, range and Doppler factors are matched, and the complex pseudo-spectrum is constructed to use additional phase information of raw data for efficient energy integration. Finally, simulation results are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in raw ambiguous range-Doppler plane of Doppler radars.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Spreading With Range Cell Migration in FMCW Automotive Radar
abstract: High range and speed resolutions provided by FMCW automotive radars are prone to range cell migration in high speed scenarios. The range and Doppler information are smeared through multiple frequency bins in fast an slowtime dimensions, resulting in biased estimations and worsened separation performance. In this paper, the FMCW signal model with inter-pulse range cell migration is derived, the induced bandwidth spreading is illustrated and quantified with simulations. Windowing is shown to mitigate this spreading.

articleTitle: ROXI: a small compact vertically-pointing X-band radar Doppler for atmospheric profiling
abstract: ROXI is a compact transportable X-band radar designed to provide long-term measurements of reflectivity and Doppler (velocity and spectra) in rainy situation. It was initially thought to perform studies on ice microphysics to address uncertainties in the retrieval of rain from satellite remote-sensing instruments. Since its deployment in Q4 2016, ROXI has been deployed in various field campaigns during which a rich dataset was acquired. In the present short paper, we present a number of possible applications of such a versatile system.

articleTitle: SAR time-series for under canopy detection
abstract: This paper reviews the techniques developed at SONDRA to detect targets under the canopy. It starts with a single SAR image with the plate detector and continues with the recent use of the SAR series. Different approaches are described for the latter, whether using azimuthal diversity or variation in the time series at a pixel level. We illustrated two methods using a short time series of SAR airborne images acquired by ONERA and applied to car detection within tropical forests.

articleTitle: An Improved Total Least Squares-Based Monopulse Ratio Estimate Given Multiple Data-Snapshots from a Uniform Line Array
abstract: We derive the Total Least Squares estimate of the monopulse ratio in noise and show its superiority over the Least Squares estimate that has been studied thus far in the literature. Such superiority occurs because the Total Least Squares estimate does not exhibit the bias introduced by noise in the Least Squares case. Regarding implementation, the Total Least Squares estimate involves a simple closed-form expression of the Σ and Δ beams.

articleTitle: Experiments with Cognitive Micro-Doppler Radar: Detection of Aircrafts’ Micro-Doppler Signals with Varied CPIs and PRFs
abstract: In our prior research, we introduced the concept of cognitive micro-Doppler radar, primarily analyzing data from small drones through experiments. This study extends our investigation to include micro-Doppler signals from larger aircrafts, marking a pioneering effort globally. We employed dynamic CPIs and PRFs within the framework of a cognitive radar system to explore these signals. To validate our approach, we captured X-band radar signals from a fixed-wing plane (P750) and a helicopter (AS350). Our experiments revealed that adjusting CPI and PRF settings can optimize the micro-Doppler signatures of both the P750 and AS350. While existing research typically relies on fixed CPI and PRF for radar detection of aircraft micro-Doppler signals, our study highlights the potential of cognitive micro-Doppler radar in aircraft detection and tracking, especially concerning micro-Doppler signatures.

articleTitle: Detection of wheelchairs in indoor and public spaces using an LTE-based passive radar
abstract: This study explores the potential of leveraging Long Term Evolution (LTE) as an illuminator of opportunity, combined with Machine Learning (ML), to detect the presence of objects in the nearby environment. Specifically, the research focuses on detecting wheelchairs. The machine learning algorithm is trained on datasets generated from the Master Information Block (MIB) and Signal Information Block 1 (SIB1). The data was collected using a software-defined radio (SDR) tuned to LTE band 3. The experimental results showed that an LTE-based passive SDR system can detect the presence of a wheelchair as well as other large objects within a room with a high degree of accuracy.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an Agile L-Band Frequency Synthesiser for Modern Radar Systems
abstract: Frequency Synthesisers are vital for any communication or radar system. Synthesizer performance is the linchpin of the total system performance. This paper proposes designing and implementing an agile L-Band frequency synthesizer for modern radar systems. Design parameters, simulation, and implementation results are presented. The proposed design with modulation capability enables another dimension of using an RF synthesizer not only as a local oscillator for up and down conversion but also as an RF waveform generator. This paper also, discusses the synthesizer design challenges and performance analysis, such as phase noise analysis, output power variation, and SFDR within the synthesizer band.

articleTitle: Exploring Short-Term Bird Behavior in a Local Area Using Phased-Array Avian Radar
abstract: Radar ornithology traditionally relies on weather surveillance radar systems to study bird migration patterns over large geographic areas and extended timeframes. However, there is a scarcity of information regarding short-term bird behavior in localized regions. Here, we investigate the time budgets of birds of various sizes in Tongguan County within China's Yellow River wetland bird protection area. Employing a Ku-band phased-array radar enhances our ability to efficiently observe radar signals from both small and large avian species. Our observations reveal that small birds dominate the study site, and distinct diurnal variations in time budgets exist between small and large birds, with larger species exhibiting reduced activity during the afternoon. Furthermore, the overlap of signal amplitudes between small and large birds within a single radar resolution cell challenges the radar cross-section (RCS) as a reliable classification signature. This study underscores the potential of avian radar systems utilizing phased-array radar technology as supplementary remote sensing tools for investigating bird behavior in radar ornithology.

articleTitle: Synthetic RAW data generator for ESA HARMONY mission
abstract: In this paper, we introduce HEEPS/MARE, the end-to-end simulator developed for the SAR oceanographic products of ESA Earth Explorer 10 mission, Harmony, expected to launch in Decembre 2029. Harmony is primarily dedicated to the observation of small-scale motion and deformation fields of the Earth surface (oceans, glaciers and ice sheets, solid Earth), thanks to passive SAR/ATI receivers carried by two companion satellites for Sentinel-1. The paper focuses on the raw data generator designed to efficiently simulate large, heterogeneous, moving oceanic areas and produce the acquired SAR/ATI bistatic IQ signals. The heterogeneous sea-surface model, bistatic scattering model, multi-GPU implementation and achieved performance are emphasized. Finally, sample results are presented, to illustrate the ability of Harmony to map wind and surface current vectors at kilometric scale.

articleTitle: Symplectic Geometry in Radar: 2-Form of Maxwell Equations and Wigner/Woodward Ambiguity Function
abstract: We will introduce the symplectic geometry structures that appear naturally in two radar application domains. We will start, in a first part, by introducing the closed 2-form for the Maxwell equations characterizing the symplectic manifold structure associated with the electromagnetic wave equations. In a second part, we will consider the Woodward Radar self-ambiguity function through Wigner function, in the case of the Heisenberg-Weyl symmetry group. The Wigner function is then defined on the coadjoint orbit (action of the Lie group on the dual of its Lie algebra), with a Liouville invariant measure (invariant measures under the group action) and a symplectic structure that make them geometrically similar to classical phase spaces. This ensures its interpretation as a quasi-distribution on a phase space. We will recall in introduction a synthetical history of Symplectic Geometry and its introduction by Jean-Marie Souriau in a seminal paper in 1953 to geometrize classical Mechanics based on Lagrange bracket.

articleTitle: Non-coherent Cognitive Technique For Frequency Selective Jamming
abstract: This paper deals with the design of non-coherent jamming strategies capable of ensuring spectral compatibility with friendly radio frequency (RF) emitters. The desired goal is achieved via a cognitive approach, which, after recognizing the presence of friendly RF systems within the bandwidth of interest (perception), synthesizes a barrage jamming waveform (action) with spectral notches, that allows to interfere exclusively with opposite emissions. Two methods are proposed for the design of the jamming signal. The former leverages optimization techniques for quadratically constrained quadratic problems (QCQP) where each constraint embeds the interference level tolerable by a specific friendly RF system. The latter is a very computationally efficient approach based on simple projections, allowing a control over the spectral notch positions and widths. At the analysis stage, the performance of the devised jamming techniques is firstly numerically analyzed in terms of spectral occupancy and autocorrelation characteristics. Finally, the process of waveform transmission and reception is also experimentally assessed with software defined radio (SDR) devices.

articleTitle: Training Deep Learning Models with Hybrid Datasets for Robust Automatic Target Detection on real SAR images
abstract: In this work, we propose to tackle several challenges hindering the development of Automatic Target Detection (ATD) algorithms for ground targets in SAR images. To address the lack of representative training data, we propose a Deep Learning approach to train ATD models with synthetic target signatures produced with the MOCEM simulator. We define an incrustation pipeline to incorporate synthetic targets into real backgrounds. Using this hybrid dataset, we train ATD models specifically tailored to bridge the domain gap between synthetic and real data. Our approach notably relies on massive physics-based data augmentation techniques and Adversarial Training of two deep-learning detection architectures. We then test these models on several datasets, including (1) patchworks of real SAR images, (2) images with the incrustation of real targets in real backgrounds, and (3) images with the incrustation of synthetic background objects in real backgrounds. Results show that the produced hybrid datasets are exempt from image overlay bias. Our approach can reach up to 90% of Average Precision on real data while exclusively using synthetic targets for training.

articleTitle: Sparse Vector-Antenna Array Design for Dual-Functional Radar Communications
abstract: Dual functional radar communications (DFRC) has gained increased attention in both academia and industry due to its recognized prominence to alleviate the spectrum congestion. The key to the DFRC design is the separation between radar and communication signals, for example, in either time, frequency or spatial domain for most existing methods in the literature. In this work, we consider the design of DFRC systems using an array of vector-antennas, which consists of P ≥ 2 orthogonal electric or magnetic dipole elements. To reduce the system cost caused by a complete front-end associated with each dipole, we further consider the sparse vector-antenna array design, which jointly optimizes the vector-antenna positions, the compositon of dipoles and the beamforming weights. The communication capacity can be doubled via modulating the complex beampattern in both H-and V-plane. Most importantly, the mutual interference between radar and communication can be mitigated when the polarizations of the beampattern towards the target and communication user are orthogonal to each other. Simulation results show that both the beampattern shape and polarization can be controlled using sparse vector-antenna arrays for DFRC applications.

articleTitle: Wavefield Networked Sensing for High-Resolution Distributed Automotive Microwave Imaging
abstract: Coherent multistatic radio imaging is an appealing concept for the forthcoming generation of wireless networks, involving distributed nodes that cooperate to achieve accurate sensing resolution and robustness. This paper presents an application of this concept tailored to the case of vehicular radar networks. The considered scenario assumes a system composed of a number of vehicles equipped with low-performance Radars, operating simultaneously in different frequency channels. On request by one user, all vehicles enter in cooperation mode to receive the echoes produced by the targets in response to all transmitted signals. This mechanism results in the vehicle formation to act as a single distributed multistatic Radar, allowing for a dramatic improvement of spatial resolution. Coherent multistatic processing is enabled by a careful three-step phase synchronization procedure, mandatorily required to synchronize individual oscillators to within a fraction of the carrier cycle and correct navigational data to within a fraction of the carrier wavelength. We demonstrate the significant benefits of cooperative coherent imaging in the considered automotive scenario in terms of both probability of correct detection, evaluated considering several system parameters, as well as resolution capabilities, showcased by experimental results from a dedicated acquisition campaign wherein the cooperation between two vehicles enables the detection of the legs of a pedestrian in close proximity to a parked car.

articleTitle: Target Focused Estimation of the Stages in the Multistage Wiener Filter
abstract: Adaptive detection techniques for airborne radar suffer in non-stationary, non-homogeneous environments and when there is limited sample support. The multistage Wiener filter (MWF) is a reduced rank adaptive detector that reduces the required sample support while lowering the computational burden. Key to these benefits is the provision of a reliable method to determine the number of MWF stages. Current approaches estimate the rank of the entire clutter subspace, which often overestimates the number of MWF stages. Consequently, we reformulate the problem and propose an algorithm that determines the number of stages required to achieve the maximum probability of detection. The algorithm is formulated as a model order estimation problem and utilises log-likelihood ratios. We provide a computationally efficient implementation and demonstrate its effectiveness through simulations.

articleTitle: Segmentation and Classification of Solid Construction Waste with mmWave Imaging
abstract: Solid construction waste is imposing a significant weight on both society and the natural environment. For solid waste segmentation and classification, the preferred method is optical imaging. However, the dust and rain can cause attenuation and obscure light for optical imaging. This paper primarily delves into the resource recycling for solid waste using mmWave imaging segmentation methods which weather and dust have little effect on. We propose an intelligent identification method for solid construction waste based on millimeter wave SAR imaging and an improved U-Net network. Our experiments show that mmWave imaging can be used in obstruct cases for solid waste imaging. With improved U-Net and data enhancement methods, we efficiently tackled the solid waste identification issue in construction and achieved over 84% segmentation accuracy on average for 5 classes.

articleTitle: Differential evolution algorithm to jointly estimate the target parameters in a MIMO OFDM DFRC system
abstract: When dealing with dual-function Radar and communication systems equipped with multiple antennas and based on orthogonal frequency division multiplexing, the target parameters, i.e., the direction of arrival (DOA), the range and the velocity have to be estimated. In some approaches like those based on the Fourier transform, the estimations of the range and the velocity require the DOA estimates beforehand. This can be problematic if the DOA estimation is not accurate enough. In others like those based on subspace methods, the target parameters can be estimated independently, but a posteriori pairing of the parameter estimates for each target is required along with constraints on the data to be transmitted. In this paper, to avoid the above issues, we suggest analyzing the relevance of the joint estimation of the target parameters by using an evolutionary algorithm like a differential-evolution based method. In that case, various aspects must be addressed such as the definition of the loss function, the selection of the stopping criterion and the tuning of the control parameters. However, a question remains: to what extent can we have confidence in the solution obtained after convergence of the algorithm? For this reason, we selected a loss function allowing us to add a final step to check whether the parameter estimation can be relevant or not. Finally, we present some results of the proposed method and discuss its limitations related to the number of targets in relation to the number of observations available.
